notes: TBox rule edit (verifier rebuild: the writer's rule 'every planet of the Solar System orbits the Sun' was re-picked, because Mars or Jupiter orbiting Earth contradicts firm facts outside the chain (their periods around the Sun, Kepler's laws, the transfer orbits of missions to Mars), and Mars orbiting the Sun while not being a planet contradicts the eight-planet Solar System). Derivability very_unlikely: the rule is the definition of a first-class lever, stated in general form in textbooks and Wikipedia ('first class lever' 1,681 in Dolma). No exceptions: the class is defined by the fulcrum's position. Counterfactual: the load in the middle is the second-class lever (a plausible confusion), clearly false. Determinate queries use invented tools named in the prompt (Brannick grip, Tollan arm). Indeterminate queries use the two textbook examples whose layout everyone also knows by sight: the seesaw (pivot between the riders) and scissors (pivot between handles and blades). The crowbar was avoided because it is used as a first- or a second-class lever. Two independent choices, four worlds. Step 3: in the name worlds the seesaw or the scissors stop being first-class levers, a textbook label; this contradicts no fact about anything outside the chain. The rule worlds contradict only the member's own layout (the stored fact that gives way); they are lopsided and kept (decision 4). Near query (third-class lever: the effort is in the middle) is unaffected and differs from the new answer.
